translations.kjv: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.
translations.ylt: James, of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ a servant, to the Twelve Tribes who are in the dispersion: Hail!
translations.web: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are in the Dispersion: Greetings.

translations.kjv: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations;
translations.ylt: All joy count it, my brethren, when ye may fall into temptations manifold;
translations.web: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations,

translations.kjv: Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.
translations.ylt: knowing that the proof of your faith doth work endurance,
translations.web: knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.

translations.kjv: But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.
translations.ylt: and let the endurance have a perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire--in nothing lacking;
translations.web: Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.

translations.kjv: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
translations.ylt: and if any of you do lack wisdom, let him ask from God, who is giving to all liberally, and not reproaching, and it shall be given to him;
translations.web: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.

translations.kjv: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.
translations.ylt: and let him ask in faith, nothing doubting, for he who is doubting hath been like a wave of the sea, driven by wind and tossed,
translations.web: But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed.

translations.kjv: For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.
translations.ylt: for let not that man suppose that he shall receive anything from the Lord--
translations.web: For that man shouldn’t think that he will receive anything from the Lord.

translations.kjv: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.
translations.ylt: a two-souled man is unstable in all his ways.
translations.web: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.

translations.kjv: Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted:
translations.ylt: And let the brother who is low rejoice in his exaltation,
translations.web: Let the brother in humble circumstances glory in his high position;

translations.kjv: But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.
translations.ylt: and the rich in his becoming low, because as a flower of grass he shall pass away;
translations.web: and the rich, in that he is made humble, because like the flower in the grass, he will pass away.

translations.kjv: For the sun is no sooner risen with a burning heat, but it withereth the grass, and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways.
translations.ylt: for the sun did rise with the burning heat, and did wither the grass, and the flower of it fell, and the grace of its appearance did perish, so also the rich in his way shall fade away!
translations.web: For the sun arises with the scorching wind and withers the grass; and the flower in it falls, and the beauty of its appearance perishes. So the rich man will also fade away in his pursuits.

translations.kjv: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.
translations.ylt: Happy the man who doth endure temptation, because, becoming approved, he shall receive the crown of the life, which the Lord did promise to those loving Him.
translations.web: Blessed is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those who love him.

translations.kjv: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:
translations.ylt: Let no one say, being tempted--`From God I am tempted,' for God is not tempted of evil, and Himself doth tempt no one,
translations.web: Let no man say when he is tempted, “I am tempted by God,” for God can’t be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.

translations.kjv: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.
translations.ylt: and each one is tempted, by his own desires being led away and enticed,
translations.web: But each one is tempted when he is drawn away by his own lust and enticed.

translations.kjv: Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.
translations.ylt: afterward the desire having conceived, doth give birth to sin, and the sin having been perfected, doth bring forth death.
translations.web: Then the lust, when it has conceived, bears sin. The sin, when it is full grown, produces death.

translations.kjv: Do not err, my beloved brethren.
translations.ylt: Be not led astray, my brethren beloved;
translations.web: Don’t be deceived, my beloved brothers.

translations.kjv: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
translations.ylt: every good giving, and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the lights, with whom is no variation, or shadow of turning;
translations.web: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation nor turning shadow.

translations.kjv: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
translations.ylt: having counselled, He did beget us with a word of truth, for our being a certain first-fruit of His creatures.
translations.web: Of his own will he gave birth to us by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creatures.

translations.kjv: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
translations.ylt: So then, my brethren beloved, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger,
translations.web: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;

translations.kjv: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.
translations.ylt: for the wrath of a man the righteousness of God doth not work;
translations.web: for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.

translations.kjv: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.
translations.ylt: wherefore having put aside all filthiness and superabundance of evil, in meekness be receiving the engrafted word, that is able to save your souls;
translations.web: Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with humility the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.

translations.kjv: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
translations.ylt: and become ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves,
translations.web: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.

translations.kjv: For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass:
translations.ylt: because, if any one is a hearer of the word and not a doer, this one hath been like to a man viewing his natural face in a mirror,
translations.web: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror;

translations.kjv: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.
translations.ylt: for he did view himself, and hath gone away, and immediately he did forget of what kind he was;
translations.web: for he sees himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was.

translations.kjv: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.
translations.ylt: and he who did look into the perfect law--that of liberty, and did continue there, this one--not a forgetful hearer becoming, but a doer of work--this one shall be happy in his doing.
translations.web: But he who looks into the perfect law of freedom and continues, not being a hearer who forgets but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in what he does.

translations.kjv: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.
translations.ylt: If any one doth think to be religious among you, not bridling his tongue, but deceiving his heart, of this one vain is the religion;
translations.web: If anyone among you thinks himself to be religious while he doesn’t bridle his tongue, but deceives his heart, this man’s religion is worthless.

translations.kjv: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.
translations.ylt: religion pure and undefiled with the God and Father is this, to look after orphans and widows in their tribulation--unspotted to keep himself from the world.
translations.web: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.

translations.kjv: My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.
translations.ylt: My brethren, hold not, in respect of persons, the faith of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ,
translations.web: My brothers, don’t hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.

translations.kjv: For if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment;
translations.ylt: for if there may come into your synagogue a man with gold ring, in gay raiment, and there may come in also a poor man in vile raiment,
translations.web: For if a man with a gold ring, in fine clothing, comes into your synagogue, and a poor man in filthy clothing also comes in,

translations.kjv: And ye have respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say unto him, Sit thou here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand thou there, or sit here under my footstool:
translations.ylt: and ye may look upon him bearing the gay raiment, and may say to him, `Thou--sit thou here well,' and to the poor man may say, `Thou--stand thou there, or, Sit thou here under my footstool,' --
translations.web: and you pay special attention to him who wears the fine clothing and say, “Sit here in a good place;” and you tell the poor man, “Stand there,” or “Sit by my footstool”

translations.kjv: Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?
translations.ylt: ye did not judge fully in yourselves, and did become ill-reasoning judges.
translations.web: haven’t you shown partiality among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?

translations.kjv: Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?
translations.ylt: Hearken, my brethren beloved, did not God choose the poor of this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the reign that He promised to those loving Him?
translations.web: Listen, my beloved brothers. Didn’t God choose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom which he promised to those who love him?

translations.kjv: But ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?
translations.ylt: and ye did dishonour the poor one; do not the rich oppress you and themselves draw you to judgment-seats;
translations.web: But you have dishonored the poor man. Don’t the rich oppress you and personally drag you before the courts?

translations.kjv: Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?
translations.ylt: do they not themselves speak evil of the good name that was called upon you?
translations.web: Don’t they blaspheme the honorable name by which you are called?

translations.kjv: If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well:
translations.ylt: If, indeed, royal law ye complete, according to the Writing, `Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself,' --ye do well;
translations.web: However, if you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.

translations.kjv: But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.
translations.ylt: and if ye accept persons, sin ye do work, being convicted by the law as transgressors;
translations.web: But if you show partiality, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.

translations.kjv: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.
translations.ylt: for whoever the whole law shall keep, and shall stumble in one point, he hath become guilty of all;
translations.web: For whoever keeps the whole law, and yet stumbles in one point, he has become guilty of all.

translations.kjv: For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law.
translations.ylt: for He who is saying, `Thou mayest not commit adultery,' said also, `Thou mayest do no murder;' and if thou shalt not commit adultery, and shalt commit murder, thou hast become a transgressor of law;
translations.web: For he who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not commit murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.

translations.kjv: So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.
translations.ylt: so speak ye and so do, as about by a law of liberty to be judged,
translations.web: So speak and so do as men who are to be judged by the law of freedom.

translations.kjv: For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.
translations.ylt: for the judgment without kindness is to him not having done kindness, and exult doth kindness over judgment.
translations.web: For judgment is without mercy to him who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.

translations.kjv: What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?
translations.ylt: What is the profit, my brethren, if faith, any one may speak of having, and works he may not have? is that faith able to save him?
translations.web: What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works? Can faith save him?

translations.kjv: If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,
translations.ylt: and if a brother or sister may be naked, and may be destitute of the daily food,
translations.web: And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food,

translations.kjv: And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?
translations.ylt: and any one of you may say to them, `Depart ye in peace, be warmed, and be filled,' and may not give to them the things needful for the body, what is the profit?
translations.web: and one of you tells them, “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled;” yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it?

translations.kjv: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.
translations.ylt: so also the faith, if it may not have works, is dead by itself.
translations.web: Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.

translations.kjv: Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.
translations.ylt: But say may some one, Thou hast faith, and I have works, shew me thy faith out of thy works, and I will shew thee out of my works my faith:
translations.web: Yes, a man will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith by my works.

translations.kjv: Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.
translations.ylt: thou--thou dost believe that God is one; thou dost well, and the demons believe, and they shudder!
translations.web: You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe—and shudder.

translations.kjv: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?
translations.ylt: And dost thou wish to know, O vain man, that the faith apart from the works is dead?
translations.web: But do you want to know, vain man, that faith apart from works is dead?

translations.kjv: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
translations.ylt: Abraham our father--was not he declared righteous out of works, having brought up Isaac his son upon the altar?
translations.web: Wasn’t Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?

translations.kjv: Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?
translations.ylt: dost thou see that the faith was working with his works, and out of the works the faith was perfected?
translations.web: You see that faith worked with his works, and by works faith was perfected.

translations.kjv: And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.
translations.ylt: and fulfilled was the Writing that is saying, `And Abraham did believe God, and it was reckoned to him--to righteousness;' and, `Friend of God' he was called.
translations.web: So the Scripture was fulfilled which says, “Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him as righteousness,” and he was called the friend of God.

translations.kjv: Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.
translations.ylt: Ye see, then, that out of works is man declared righteous, and not out of faith only;
translations.web: You see then that by works a man is justified, and not only by faith.

translations.kjv: Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?
translations.ylt: and in like manner also Rahab the harlot--was she not out of works declared righteous, having received the messengers, and by another way having sent forth?
translations.web: In the same way, wasn’t Rahab the prostitute also justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way?

translations.kjv: For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.
translations.ylt: for as the body apart from the spirit is dead, so also the faith apart from the works is dead.
translations.web: For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, even so faith apart from works is dead.

translations.kjv: My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.
translations.ylt: Many teachers become not, my brethren, having known that greater judgment we shall receive,
translations.web: Let not many of you be teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive heavier judgment.

translations.kjv: For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.
translations.ylt: for we all make many stumbles; if any one in word doth not stumble, this one is a perfect man, able to bridle also the whole body;
translations.web: For we all stumble in many things. Anyone who doesn’t stumble in word is a perfect person, able to bridle the whole body also.

translations.kjv: Behold, we put bits in the horses’ mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
translations.ylt: lo, the bits we put into the mouths of the horses for their obeying us, and their whole body we turn about;
translations.web: Indeed, we put bits into the horses’ mouths so that they may obey us, and we guide their whole body.

translations.kjv: Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth.
translations.ylt: lo, also the ships, being so great, and by fierce winds being driven, are led about by a very small helm, whithersoever the impulse of the helmsman doth counsel,
translations.web: Behold, the ships also, though they are so big and are driven by fierce winds, are yet guided by a very small rudder, wherever the pilot desires.

translations.kjv: Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!
translations.ylt: so also the tongue is a little member, and doth boast greatly; lo, a little fire how much wood it doth kindle!
translations.web: So the tongue is also a little member, and boasts great things. See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!

translations.kjv: And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.
translations.ylt: and the tongue is a fire, the world of the unrighteousness, so the tongue is set in our members, which is spotting our whole body, and is setting on fire the course of nature, and is set on fire by the gehenna.
translations.web: And the tongue is a fire. The world of iniquity among our members is the tongue, which defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of nature, and is set on fire by Gehenna.

translations.kjv: For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed of mankind:
translations.ylt: For every nature, both of beasts and of fowls, both of creeping things and things of the sea, is subdued, and hath been subdued, by the human nature,
translations.web: For every kind of animal, bird, creeping thing, and sea creature is tamed, and has been tamed by mankind;

translations.kjv: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.
translations.ylt: and the tongue no one of men is able to subdue, it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison,
translations.web: but nobody can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

translations.kjv: Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God.
translations.ylt: with it we do bless the God and Father, and with it we do curse the men made according to the similitude of God;
translations.web: With it we bless our God and Father, and with it we curse men who are made in the image of God.

translations.kjv: Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.
translations.ylt: out of the same mouth doth come forth blessing and cursing; it doth not need, my brethren, these things so to happen;
translations.web: Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so.

translations.kjv: Doth a fountain send forth at the same place sweet water and bitter?
translations.ylt: doth the fountain out of the same opening pour forth the sweet and the bitter?
translations.web: Does a spring send out from the same opening fresh and bitter water?

translations.kjv: Can the fig tree, my brethren, bear olive berries? either a vine, figs? so can no fountain both yield salt water and fresh.
translations.ylt: is a fig-tree able, my brethren, olives to make? or a vine figs? so no fountain salt and sweet water is able to make.
translations.web: Can a fig tree, my brothers, yield olives, or a vine figs? Thus no spring yields both salt water and fresh water.

translations.kjv: Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.
translations.ylt: Who is wise and intelligent among you? let him shew out of the good behaviour his works in meekness of wisdom,
translations.web: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct that his deeds are done in gentleness of wisdom.

translations.kjv: But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth.
translations.ylt: and if bitter zeal ye have, and rivalry in your heart, glory not, nor lie against the truth;
translations.web: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, don’t boast and don’t lie against the truth.

translations.kjv: This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.
translations.ylt: this wisdom is not descending from above, but earthly, physical, demon-like,
translations.web: This wisdom is not that which comes down from above, but is earthly, sensual, and demonic.

translations.kjv: For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.
translations.ylt: for where zeal and rivalry are, there is insurrection and every evil matter;
translations.web: For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed.

translations.kjv: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
translations.ylt: and the wisdom from above, first, indeed, is pure, then peaceable, gentle, easily entreated, full of kindness and good fruits, uncontentious, and unhypocritical: --
translations.web: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.

translations.kjv: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace.
translations.ylt: and the fruit of the righteousness in peace is sown to those making peace.
translations.web: Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

translations.kjv: From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?
translations.ylt: Whence are wars and fightings among you? not thence--out of your passions, that are as soldiers in your members?
translations.web: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members?

translations.kjv: Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.
translations.ylt: ye desire, and ye have not; ye murder, and are zealous, and are not able to attain; ye fight and war, and ye have not, because of your not asking;
translations.web: You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. You fight and make war. You don’t have, because you don’t ask.

translations.kjv: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.
translations.ylt: ye ask, and ye receive not, because evilly ye ask, that in your pleasures ye may spend it.
translations.web: You ask, and don’t receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.

translations.kjv: Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.
translations.ylt: Adulterers and adulteresses! have ye not known that friendship of the world is enmity with God? whoever, then, may counsel to be a friend of the world, an enemy of God he is set.
translations.web: You adulterers and adulteresses, don’t you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Whoever therefore wants to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.

translations.kjv: Do ye think that the scripture saith in vain, The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy?
translations.ylt: Do ye think that emptily the Writing saith, `To envy earnestly desireth the spirit that did dwell in us,'
translations.web: Or do you think that the Scripture says in vain, “The Spirit who lives in us yearns jealously”?

translations.kjv: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.
translations.ylt: and greater grace he doth give, wherefore he saith, `God against proud ones doth set Himself up, and to lowly ones He doth give grace?'
translations.web: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

translations.kjv: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
translations.ylt: be subject, then, to God; stand up against the devil, and he will flee from you;
translations.web: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

translations.kjv: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
translations.ylt: draw nigh to God, and He will draw nigh to you; cleanse hands, ye sinners! and purify hearts, ye two-souled!
translations.web: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.

translations.kjv: Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness.
translations.ylt: be exceeding afflicted, and mourn, and weep, let your laughter to mourning be turned, and the joy to heaviness;
translations.web: Lament, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom.

translations.kjv: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.
translations.ylt: be made low before the Lord, and He shall exalt you.
translations.web: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.

translations.kjv: Speak not evil one of another, brethren. He that speaketh evil of his brother, and judgeth his brother, speaketh evil of the law, and judgeth the law: but if thou judge the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge.
translations.ylt: Speak not one against another, brethren; he who is speaking against a brother, and is judging his brother, doth speak against law, and doth judge law, and if law thou dost judge, thou art not a doer of law but a judge;
translations.web: Don’t speak against one another, brothers. He who speaks against a brother and judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.

translations.kjv: There is one lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy: who art thou that judgest another?
translations.ylt: one is the lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy; thou--who art thou that dost judge the other?
translations.web: Only one is the lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge another?

translations.kjv: Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain:
translations.ylt: Go, now, ye who are saying, `To-day and to-morrow we will go on to such a city, and will pass there one year, and traffic, and make gain;'
translations.web: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow let’s go into this city and spend a year there, trade, and make a profit.”

translations.kjv: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
translations.ylt: who do not know the thing of the morrow; for what is your life? for it is a vapour that is appearing for a little, and then is vanishing;
translations.web: Yet you don’t know what your life will be like tomorrow. For what is your life? For you are a vapor that appears for a little time and then vanishes away.

translations.kjv: For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.
translations.ylt: instead of your saying, `If the Lord may will, we shall live, and do this or that;'
translations.web: For you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will both live, and do this or that.”

translations.kjv: But now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.
translations.ylt: and now ye glory in your pride; all such glorying is evil;
translations.web: But now you glory in your boasting. All such boasting is evil.

translations.kjv: Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.
translations.ylt: to him, then, knowing to do good, and not doing, sin it is to him.
translations.web: To him therefore who knows to do good and doesn’t do it, to him it is sin.

translations.kjv: Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.
translations.ylt: Go, now, ye rich! weep, howling over your miseries that are coming upon you;
translations.web: Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming on you.

translations.kjv: Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are motheaten.
translations.ylt: your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten;
translations.web: Your riches are corrupted and your garments are moth-eaten.

translations.kjv: Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.
translations.ylt: your gold and silver have rotted, and the rust of them for a testimony shall be to you, and shall eat your flesh as fire. Ye made treasure in the last days!
translations.web: Your gold and your silver are corroded, and their corrosion will be for a testimony against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have laid up your treasure in the last days.

translations.kjv: Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth.
translations.ylt: lo, the reward of the workmen, of those who in-gathered your fields, which hath been fraudulently kept back by you--doth cry out, and the exclamations of those who did reap into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth have entered;
translations.web: Behold, the wages of the laborers who mowed your fields, which you have kept back by fraud, cry out; and the cries of those who reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Armies.

translations.kjv: Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter.
translations.ylt: ye did live in luxury upon the earth, and were wanton; ye did nourish your hearts, as in a day of slaughter;
translations.web: You have lived in luxury on the earth, and taken your pleasure. You have nourished your hearts as in a day of slaughter.

translations.kjv: Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you.
translations.ylt: ye did condemn--ye did murder the righteous one, he doth not resist you.
translations.web: You have condemned and you have murdered the righteous one. He doesn’t resist you.

translations.kjv: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.
translations.ylt: Be patient, then, brethren, till the presence of the Lord; lo, the husbandman doth expect the precious fruit of the earth, being patient for it, till he may receive rain--early and latter;
translations.web: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receives the early and late rain.

translations.kjv: Be ye also patient; stablish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord draweth nigh.
translations.ylt: be patient, ye also; establish your hearts, because the presence of the Lord hath drawn nigh;
translations.web: You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.

translations.kjv: Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest ye be condemned: behold, the judge standeth before the door.
translations.ylt: murmur not against one another, brethren, that ye may not be condemned; lo, the Judge before the door hath stood.
translations.web: Don’t grumble, brothers, against one another, so that you won’t be judged. Behold, the judge stands at the door.

translations.kjv: Take, my brethren, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction, and of patience.
translations.ylt: An example take ye of the suffering of evil, my brethren, and of the patience, the prophets who did speak in the name of the Lord;
translations.web: Take, brothers, for an example of suffering and of perseverance, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

translations.kjv: Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.
translations.ylt: lo, we call happy those who are enduring; the endurance of Job ye heard of, and the end of the Lord ye have seen, that very compassionate is the Lord, and pitying.
translations.web: Behold, we call them blessed who endured. You have heard of the perseverance of Job and have seen the Lord in the outcome, and how the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

translations.kjv: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.
translations.ylt: And before all things, my brethren, do not swear, neither by the heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath, and let your Yes be Yes, and the No, No; that under judgment ye may not fall.
translations.web: But above all things, my brothers, don’t swear—not by heaven, or by the earth, or by any other oath; but let your “yes” be “yes”, and your “no”, “no”, so that you don’t fall into hypocrisy.

translations.kjv: Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.
translations.ylt: Doth any one suffer evil among you? let him pray; is any of good cheer? let him sing psalms;
translations.web: Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.

translations.kjv: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord:
translations.ylt: is any infirm among you? let him call for the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, having anointed him with oil, in the name of the Lord,
translations.web: Is any among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord;

translations.kjv: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.
translations.ylt: and the prayer of the faith shall save the distressed one, and the Lord shall raise him up, and if sins he may have committed, they shall be forgiven to him.
translations.web: and the prayer of faith will heal him who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.

translations.kjv: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
translations.ylt: Be confessing to one another the trespasses, and be praying for one another, that ye may be healed; very strong is a working supplication of a righteous man;
translations.web: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.

translations.kjv: Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months.
translations.ylt: Elijah was a man like affected as we, and with prayer he did pray--not to rain, and it did not rain upon the land three years and six months;
translations.web: Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it didn’t rain on the earth for three years and six months.

translations.kjv: And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.
translations.ylt: and again he did pray, and the heaven did give rain, and the land did bring forth her fruit.
translations.web: He prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth produced its fruit.

translations.kjv: Brethren, if any of you do err from the truth, and one convert him;
translations.ylt: Brethren, if any among you may go astray from the truth, and any one may turn him back,
translations.web: Brothers, if any among you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back,

translations.kjv: Let him know, that he which converteth the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins.
translations.ylt: let him know that he who did turn back a sinner from the straying of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall cover a multitude of sins.
translations.web: let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
